examples.text: move and countermove

When you're ready, just call out the position of the pieces and I'll give you a countermove.

glosses: To move in opposition or in retaliation.

glosses: An action or statement in response to a stimulus or other event.

examples.text: The announcement of the verdict brought a violent reaction.
You were in the courtroom. What is your reaction?
When I last tried to eat strawberries I had a terrible allergic reaction.

glosses: A transformation in which one or more substances is converted into another by combination or decomposition.

examples.text: In this reaction, the acid and base will neutralize each other, producing a salt.

glosses: To come or go back (to a place or person).

examples.text: Although the birds fly north for the summer, they return here in winter.

The Celebrity, by arts unknown, induced Mrs. Judge Short and two other ladies to call at Mohair on a certain afternoon when Mr. Cooke was trying a trotter on the track. The three returned wondering and charmed with Mrs. Cooke; they were sure she had had no hand in the furnishing of that atrocious house.
"I came through and I shall return," General MacArthur declared when he spoke at Terowie of the beleagured Philippines.

As soon as Julia returned with a constable, Timothy, who was on the point of exhaustion, prepared to give over to him gratefully. The newcomer turned out to be a powerful youngster, fully trained and eager to help, and he stripped off his tunic at once.

glosses: To go back in thought, narration, or argument.

examples.text: To return to my story[…]

glosses: To recur; to come again.

examples.text: Winter returns every year.

glosses: To turn back, retreat.

examples.text: ‘I suppose here is none woll be glad to returne – and as for me,’ seyde Sir Cador, ‘I had lever dye this day that onys to turne my bak.’

glosses: To turn (something) round.

examples.text: Whan Kyng Marke harde hym sey that worde, he returned his horse and abode by hym.

glosses: To place or put back something where it had been.

examples.text: Please return your hands to your lap.

glosses: To give something back to its original holder or owner.

examples.text: You should return the library book within one month.

glosses: To give in requital or recompense; to requite.

examples.text: […]the Lord ſhall returne thy wickedneſſe vpon thine owne head.

glosses: To reciprocate (a visit or telephone call).

examples.text: Hello, I'm just returning your call. What did you want to talk about?

glosses: To take back something to a vendor for a complete or partial refund.

examples.text: Yeah, it's $600,000 but, if it doesn't work, you can always return it. As long as it's undamaged and in the original packaging, I'll give you a full refund.

glosses: To bat the ball back over the net in response to a serve.

examples.text: The player couldn't return the serve because it was so fast.

glosses: To play a card as a result of another player's lead.

examples.text: If one players plays a trump, the others must return a trump.

glosses: To throw a ball back to the wicket-keeper (or a fielder at that position) from somewhere in the field.
To say in reply; to respond.

examples.text: to return an answer;  to return thanks;  "Do it yourself!" she returned.
“No!” returned the spy. “I throw up. I confess that we were so unpopular with the outrageous mob, that I only got away from England at the risk of being ducked to death […]
“Ah my good friend, I do look out,” the young man returned while Maisie helped herself afresh to bread and butter.

glosses: To relinquish control to the calling procedure.
To pass (data) back to the calling procedure.

examples.text: This function returns the number of files in the directory.

glosses: To retort; to throw back.

examples.text: to return the lie
And now, if you are a Malicious Reader, I expect you ſhould return upon me, that I affect to be thought more Impartial than I am.

glosses: To report, or bring back and make known.

examples.text: to return the result of an election
And all the people anſwered together, [...] and Moſes returned the wordes of the people vnto the Lord.

glosses: To elect according to the official report of the election officers.
To give a thrust or cut after parrying a sword-thrust.
The act of returning.

examples.text: I expect the house to be spotless upon my return.

[…] of the existence or nonexistence of parental intent to abandon a subject minor child, whether the best interests and welfare of such minor child will be served by taking custody from the parents, and whether return of a child to the parents would be detrimental to such child.

examples.text: Do you want a one-way or a return?

glosses: An item that is returned, e.g. due to a defect, or the act of returning it.

examples.text: Last year there were 250 returns of this product, an improvement on the 500 returns the year before.

glosses: An answer.

examples.text: a return to one's question

glosses: An account, or formal report, of an action performed, of a duty discharged, of facts or statistics, etc.; especially, in the plural, a set of tabulated statistics prepared for general information.

examples.text: election returns; a return of the amount of goods produced or sold
The other returns having come in, the result of the poll, that Sir James Graham had been superseded by Major Aglionby, was declared at Carlisle soon after 11 a.m.

glosses: Gain or loss from an investment.

examples.text: It yielded a return of 5%.
from the few hours we spend in prayer and the exercises of a pious life, the return is great and profitable

Liverpool have now won only five of their 17 home league games this season. It is a poor return for a team of Liverpool's pedigree and resources but, once again, Kenny Dalglish's team were the instigators of their own downfall as chance after chance went begging.

Investors face a quandary. Cash offers a return of virtually zero in many developed countries; government-bond yields may have risen in recent weeks but they are still unattractive. Equities have suffered two big bear markets since 2000 and are wobbling again. It is hardly surprising that pension funds, insurers and endowments are searching for new sources of return.

glosses: A report of income submitted to a government for purposes of specifying exact tax payment amounts; a tax return.

examples.text: Hand in your return within 90 days of the end of the tax year.

examples.text: The boiler technician had to cut out the heating return to access the safety valve.

The act of catching a ball after a punt and running it back towards the opposing team.

examples.text: A facade of sixty feet east and west has a return of twenty feet north and south.
